title: Model Quality Regression & Evaluation Dataset Custody Addendum
body:
Purpose and scope:
This addendum is intended to be appended to Redwood Inference’s standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Data Processing Addendum (DPA) when the parties expect the customer to rely on vendor-provided model evaluations or when model regressions may trigger remediation, rollback, or credits. The addendum defines custody, preservation, access, and verification procedures for evaluation artifacts (datasets, harnesses, logs, seed-configs, and resulting metrics) that are relevant to disputed model quality changes, and the governance for escrow and transfer where required by the commercial terms.

Applicability and definitions:
- "Evaluation Artifacts": datasets used for benchmark/eval runs, test harness code, seed/config files, synthetic data generators, metric outputs (raw token logs, scores, confusion matrices), and the exact model version identifiers and weights checksums used in a run.
- "Custody Window": the period during which the Vendor must preserve Evaluation Artifacts for a particular customer or tenant.
- "Customer Audit Trigger": a documented event (e.g., measured regression > X% on a designated metric, incident report, or contractual SLA breach) that permits the Customer to request access and verification.
- "Escrow Agent": mutually agreed neutral third party for secure custody of artifacts where contractually required.

Preservation obligations (Vendor):
1) For any model version that is used to serve Customer traffic and that has been associated with Customer-specific evaluation (either by Customer or Vendor-run test suites), Vendor will preserve the associated Evaluation Artifacts for a minimum Custody Window of 18 months from the later of (a) the model version deprecation date or (b) the date of the evaluation run that generated the artifact.
2) Preservation must ensure cryptographic integrity: all model weight files, dataset files, and harness configs will have SHA-256 (or stronger) digests recorded and retained with the artifacts.
3) For ephemeral or streaming evaluation outputs (e.g., streaming token logs), Vendor will preserve the minimal raw output needed to reproduce the reported metric and the deterministic seed/seed-state used at evaluation time. If minimal raw output would include PII, Vendor will provide a pseudonymized extract with redaction metadata sufficient for auditing while protecting data subject rights.

Access and verification (Customer rights):
1) Customer Audit Trigger: upon a documented regression meeting the threshold in the SOW (statement of work) or as an SLA incident, Customer may request: (a) read access to preserved artifacts; (b) reproduction instructions and environment manifest; and (c) a Vendor-run re-evaluation under a jointly agreed harness, or a procedure for third-party verification.
2) Access modalities: Vendor will provide access via one of the following, chosen by Customer: (a) secure temporary workspace access (VPC-hosted, tenant-isolated) with policy-limited credentials; (b) secure export of artifacts to Customer’s designated S3-compatible bucket; or (c) engagement of the Escrow Agent to deliver artifacts under an agreed release protocol.
3) Time-to-access: Vendor will acknowledge an Audit Trigger within 4 business hours and provide initial access within 10 business days; if expedited access is contractually required (e.g., for high-severity SLA incidents), timelines will be set forth in the SOW.

Third-party verification and escrow:
1) If Customer requests third-party verification, Vendor will cooperate to either (a) run the agreed evaluation in a mutually audited environment and produce signed results with digests; or (b) release artifacts to the Escrow Agent with a documented chain-of-custody so that the third party can run the verification.
2) When escrow is invoked per the contract (typically for regulated customers or when the Customer makes a verified, high-impact claim about regressions), the parties will select an Escrow Agent from an approved whitelist and execute an escrow accession schedule. The escrow deposit must include: checksummed model weights, the exact harness (with version pins), the evaluation dataset (or a legally cleared pseudonymized variant), and run manifests.

Data protection and PII handling:
1) Any evaluation dataset containing PII or personal data must be handled under the DPA controls: maintain encryption at rest and in transit, log access, and honor Data Subject Requests (DSRs) where applicable.
2) Where data minimization is applicable, the Vendor will provide a pseudonymized copy for audit purposes and retain a mapping under the Customer’s control when required; the mapping is not to be used for model training or general access absent explicit Customer consent.

Reproducibility standards and required artifacts:
To permit meaningful verification, preserved artifacts should include, at minimum:
- exact model version identifier and weight checksum (SHA-256)
- evaluation script and harness version (Git commit SHA)
- deterministic seed configuration and environment manifest (OS, container image sha, library versions)
- raw metric outputs and the code that turns raw outputs into the reported metrics
- dataset version and provenance statement (including any redaction/pseudonymization steps)

Metric disputes and remediation ladder:
1) If Customer’s re-evaluation reproduces a regression that crosses the contractual threshold, the following remediation ladder applies unless the parties agree otherwise in the SOW:
   a) Hotfix or config rollback: Vendor may offer a patch or revert to the prior model variant for immediate mitigation with continued investigation.
   b) Canary rollback & phased redeploy: Vendor coordinates a rollback plan and timeline and provides monitoring hooks to Customer.
   c) Monetary remedy: if rollback or mitigation fails to restore contracted performance within the agreed remediation window, monetary credits or termination rights may apply consistent with the MSA schedule for SLA credits.
2) Root cause investigation: Vendor will produce a written RCA within 15 business days post-verification and include artifact provenance, a timeline of changes, and proposed remediation.

Retention exceptions and legal holds:
1) Vendor may purge artifacts after the Custody Window unless a Customer or regulator issues written notice requiring extended retention.
2) Legal holds: upon notice of litigation or regulatory inquiry involving the preserved artifacts, Vendor will not delete relevant artifacts and will notify Customer within 2 business days.

Subprocessor obligations:
Vendor shall ensure that any subprocessor that stores or processes Evaluation Artifacts agrees to the same preservation, access, and audit cooperation obligations as set out here. Vendor remains fully liable for subprocessor compliance.

Security, authenticity, and tamper-evidence:
- Artifacts delivered for audits or escrow must include signed manifests (vendor key or escrow agent signature) and cryptographic digests. The parties can agree to use hardware-backed signing (HSM) for high-sensitivity deposits.

Operational notes and internal playbook (for Redwood reviewers):
- Suggested threshold language for SOW: "A regression is any material deterioration in the agreed primary metric exceeding 5% relative or 0.02 absolute (whichever is larger) over a rolling 7-day window, as measured on the mutually agreed evaluation harness." (Adjustable per customer).
- Practical preservation tips: compress datasets, store checksums in the audit log, maintain a mapping table to the Customer’s tenant id and model variant, and tag artifacts with a causal label (deploy/release id, flag toggles).
- Review: coordinate with Product (Hosted API) to ensure the runtime can produce reproducible harness runs and with SRE to surface the relevant telemetry streams tied to evaluation metrics.

Drafting notes and redlines to consider (internal):
- Decide whether 18 months is the default custody period or a negotiable value in the SOW; consider GDPR data minimization impacts.
- Clarify cost allocation for escrow deposits, third-party verification fees, and transfer bandwidth. Typically the requesting party covers third-party verification costs unless regression is Vendor-attributed.
- Align timeline for Vendor-supplied RCA with contractual SLA incident windows.

Sample clause for insertion into MSA (short form):
"Model Quality Addendum: Vendor will preserve Evaluation Artifacts for the Custody Window and provide access to Customer upon a Customer Audit Trigger. Vendor will provide cryptographically signed manifests and cooperate in third-party verification. Costs for escrow or third-party verification will be allocated as set forth in the SOW."

Action items for legal/product review:
- Legal: confirm liability language and whether escrow triggers should be unilateral or mutual.
- Product: identify default metric thresholds and the standard harness we will offer for baseline verification.
- Ops/SRE: identify storage capacity impact and propose operational retention/archival architecture.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive to reduce debate at commercial negotiation time. The goal is to provide a standard addendum that can be attached to enterprise SOWs where customers need stronger artifact custody guarantees and clear auditability.

Appendix A — Checklist for preservation package (template to populate per-case):
- Model weights: filename, size, sha256
- Model manifest: architecture, tokenizer, config json
- Harness: repo URL, commit SHA, run script, container image sha
- Dataset: filename, provenance statement, pseudonymization notes if applicable
- Run manifest: date/time, runtime environment, seed config, operator id
- Metric outputs: raw output file, processing script, final metrics csv
- Signed manifest: vendor signature, timestamp

End of addendum draft.

-- Internal distribution: share with commercial-ops, legal-enterprise, product-hosted-api, eng-served-runtime for comments.

Reviewer comments history:
- 2025-01-15: Liam O'Connor — suggested shortening default custody window to 12 months for non-regulated SMBs; left as negotiable in SOW.
- 2025-01-29: Priya Desai — redline to require pseudonymization mapping held under customer control; accepted and added to PII handling section.
